title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become vigiliaGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen.
check: Measured across every shape in the running editor: Frosted glass is enabled on Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon, and aria-disabled on Polyline and Line with the reason on focus. A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click, and the Glass blur control appears only after that.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail: The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

title: The editor still does not refit the theme when the window is resized
detail: FILED SEPARATELY BECAUSE IT SURVIVED THE FIX FOR vg-068, and measured by hand rather than taken from the agent's report. Open the editor at 2048 wide and the zoom badge reads 83%. Resize the window to 1600 and it reads 83%; to 1280, still 83%; to 1024, still 83%. One number across a 1024-pixel change, while the canvas behind it goes 1394, 946, 626, 370. Click Zoom to fit at that last size and the badge reads 22% - so the fit calculation is right and something else has to ask for it. THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT IS WHICH EVENT FIRES THE REFIT. cde9aa6 made a PANEL COLLAPSE refit, and that works: at 1024, hiding the layer panel takes the canvas 370 to 658 and the zoom 22% to 39%. A WINDOW RESIZE is a different event and did not get the same treatment. This is the half that matters in ordinary use, because a deliberate panel toggle is rare and resizing a window - or opening it at a size and keeping it - is what everyone does. An author whose window is not the width they opened the editor at spends the session looking at a theme at the wrong zoom inside a black field, and the badge reads a confident number throughout. Nothing recomputes on resize; only the click recomputes it. A ResizeObserver already exists on the body in this app for other purposes, so the seam is present. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, and the reason it was reverted is the useful part. CONFIRMED EXACTLY AS FILED: at 2048 the badge reads 83% with the canvas at 1394; resize to 1024 and it still reads 83% with the canvas at 370, and the artboard still starts at x 98, so 1290 of its 1388 pixels run off the right edge. Zoom to fit at that size gives 22%, so the fit exists — it is just not automatic. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Holding the zoom and re-centring the translation on every resize does exactly what the row wants — measured, at 370 the board then spans -512 to 882 against a 370 canvas, so it is centred and the rest is reachable by panning — and it BREAKS keeps the point under the cursor fixed while zooming, which resize() calls on construction and on every host size change. Panning to inspect a corner and then any resize, spurious or not, yanks the camera back to centre. That test failing is the finding, not an accident of the harness. So the question is not how to re-centre but WHEN: only when the camera was showing the whole board, so an authors pan survives and a fitted view follows the window. That needs a condition on the previous camera state — was it fitted or contained — which the viewport does not currently keep. Reverted rather than shipped: a camera that cannot be left where the author put it is a worse defect than one that leaves part of the board off the edge.

title: Selecting a colour stutters badly: nine main-thread stalls across one drag
detail: RAISED BY THE USER as visible lag and stuttering when selecting colours, and measured rather than taken on trust - with the honest caveat that it does not reproduce on every run, which is itself part of what makes it hard to pin down. MEASURED, dragging the saturation square at roughly a human cadence - 20 moves with 40 ms between them, 3.05 seconds of dragging: nine long tasks, durations 93, 68, 76, 50, 81, 60, 77, 88 and 59 milliseconds, totalling 652 ms, maximum 93. That is 21% of the drag time with the main thread blocked, and the stalls are spread across the drag rather than bunched, so the author feels every few pixels. It was measured on Frosted panel, which eight objects use, so one colour change re-renders eight frosted surfaces - the likely shape of the cost, though I did NOT establish that: repeating the drag on tokens with 1, 8 and 28 uses produced no long tasks at all in that run, so the scaling is unconfirmed and the cause is not established here. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: this is the interaction an author repeats most in the palette panel, a deliberate drag rather than a click, so per-move cost is exactly the wrong thing to be expensive. It also composes with vg-080 - the picker is already jumping under the author's cursor, and now the drag stutters as well, so the two together make the colour control feel broken rather than merely awkward. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the same drag measured on a token with few uses against Frosted panel's eight, a few runs each, since one clean run and one clean run that measured nothing is not yet a comparison. REPEATED, AND THE VARIANCE IS PART OF THE FINDING. Re-measured with the preserved probe (docs/product/probes/longtask.mjs, which now exists because this row needed it) after the editor had been rebuilt with more work in the palette: 40% blocked with 19 long tasks peaking at 137ms, then 27% with 12 tasks peaking at 155ms, then 56% with 27 tasks peaking at 123ms. Add the original 21% and the range is 21% to 56% across four runs of the same drag, with individual stalls reaching 155ms. No build was running during the repeats, so machine load does not obviously explain it, though on a shared machine I cannot rule that out from here. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: a single measurement will not settle it and a run that happens to come back clean does not mean the author's report is wrong. The number to beat is the low end of that range, and the useful test is a drag repeated until it is fast, not once. The fact that a first run measured 21% and later runs measured two to nearly three times that is itself consistent with something in the path being intermittent rather than uniformly slow - which is the same shape of problem as vg-028's unreproduced chart slide, and the same reason both rows stay open rather than closing on a clean run. MEASURED AGAIN AFTER vg-080, and IT IS NOT FIXED BY THAT WORK, so it stays open on its own evidence rather than on a guess. Same instrument (PerformanceObserver longtask, the one docs/product/probes/longtask.mjs keeps), same 20 moves at 40 ms, same Frosted panel token with its 8 uses, viewport 2048x962: 38% blocked over 18 tasks, 44% over 24, 48% over 25 - inside the 21% to 56% range above. WHAT DID CHANGE IS THE SHAPE: the peaks the row recorded at 93, 123, 137 and 155 ms are gone and every task now lands between 50 and 57 ms with a few at 66 and 81. A run that used to spend a fifth of a second in one block now spends it in a fifth of a second in many. Two rebuilds of the whole palette field set per commit are no longer in that path, which is the most that change can be credited with; whatever costs 50 ms at a time is something else and this work did not reach it. A TRAP FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP NEXT, which cost this run its second half: installing a PerformanceObserver per run stacks every earlier observer onto the same array, and the counts climb past 100% blocked share within three drags (96, then 192, then 300 tasks over one ~2.8 s drag). Install one observer, clear the array between runs, and distrust any share above 100%. The token comparison this row asks for is still the open question - 1 use against 8 was attempted here and produced no usable comparison, because of that trap, so the scaling is still unconfirmed.

title: A chart's aspect ratio changes its height but the inspector's Height field never updates
detail: MEASURED AS A DIRECT COMPARISON after a wrong first reading, which is worth recording because it nearly cost this row. I first concluded the three ratio buttons did nothing: geometry stayed 963x215 through 3:1, 4:1 and 2:1, and the buttons had no aria-pressed, no class and no computed-style difference. Both halves of that were instrument error. The style half: the screenshot showed 3:1 boxed after I had clicked 4:1, and I had sampled backgroundColor, which is rgb(245, 241, 232) on all three - the visible box is the focus ring, and there is genuinely no selected state. The effect half: I read the chart before saving, so the document had not caught up. THE FEATURE WORKS. Save after each click and the host's document gives the truth: 4:1 takes the height 215 to 241, 3:1 to 321, 2:1 to 482, all at width 963 - exactly the ratios named. THE DEFECT IS THE INSPECTOR DISAGREES WITH ALL OF IT. Across every click the Height field in the selection inspector reads 215, unchanged, while the object it is describing is 241, then 321, then 482. Four consecutive comparisons, mismatch on every one. So an author sets 2:1, watches the chart double in height, and reads a Height field that still says 215 - and the canvas dock and the field that owns the geometry are telling them two different things about the same object. That is the same class as the layer list disagreeing with the document, and it is the more dangerous of the two here, because the Height field is editable: an author who reads 215, believes it, and types a height is editing against a number the product no longer holds. The second half is small and cheap and worth doing alongside: nothing in the control group says which ratio is active - no aria-pressed on any of the three, no class, no style difference at all - so after clicking there is no way to tell 2:1 was applied from 3:1.

title: A saved theme can never be deleted, so the library only grows
detail: CHECKED ON BOTH SIDES, because a missing button and a missing capability are different rows. On the settings page - the one surface that lists the library - the entire set of visible controls is Open the editor, the Starter template link, the theme's own button, and Edit. Nothing anywhere reads delete, remove, trash or discard. The File menu offers New theme, New from starter, Open package, Save package, Release package, Open library and Save to library, and none of them removes a theme either. So an author who has been iterating can see every experiment they have ever made in their library and cannot remove any of them. The API is not the missing half: DELETE on a theme returns 405 Method Not Allowed, so the host does not expose deletion either - this is absent by design or by omission, not merely unlinked from a UI. THE COUNTER-CLAIM I WOULD RAISE AGAINST MY OWN ROW, recorded because it is a real one and because a theme is a folder on disk (ADR-0017), so deleting one is a destructive filesystem operation with no undo. That may well be why it is not there, and I have NOT established that it is an oversight rather than a decision - which is exactly what makes this a question rather than a defect report. What I can say is what the author meets today: a list with no prune, on a product whose own File menu has Rename, Save as and Activate either available or explicitly named as missing work (vg-034), so the author is being told the management verbs exist. If deletion is deliberately out of scope, the settings page is the place that should say so, because right now the absence reads as an oversight to anyone who has not read the ADR.

title: The View menu's three settings silently cycle between two unnamed states, one of which is 1 FPS
detail: MEASURED BY CLICKING THROUGH EACH CYCLE, which is what it took to discover they are cycles at all. The View menu has three items and they read as settings - Data source: Preview, Chart refresh: 30 FPS, Value runs: values. None opens a submenu: aria-haspopup and aria-expanded are both null, and clicking one closes the menu and changes the label. Clicking each seven times in turn gives the complete cycles. Data source alternates Preview and Live. Value runs alternates values and tokens. Chart refresh alternates 30 FPS and 1 FPS. That is every value each offers. THREE PROBLEMS, and the third is the one an author would file. THE CHOICES ARE NEVER SHOWN. A menu item that toggles gives the author no way to know what the other state is, what it does, or that it exists - they can only click and read the label afterwards. A submenu, a radio group, or even a confirmation would all answer it; none does. ONE OF THE STATES IS THIRTY TIMES WORSE. Chart refresh goes from 30 FPS to 1 FPS on a single click. An author reaching into the View menu for one setting and mis-clicking lands in a preview that updates once a second, which reads as the editor hanging, and nothing on screen says why it got slow or that a second click fixes it. THE STATE IS NOT EXPOSED. No aria-checked on any of the three, so a screen reader announces a plain menu item and never says which of the two states is current - and the label text, which is the only thing carrying the state, is what a screen reader is least likely to re-read on focus. The honest comparison is one click away: the zoom badge offers Zoom to fit, Zoom to selection and 100 % as a real submenu with three visible items, so the menu is not uniformly ignorant of the pattern - these three are.

title: Layer rows declare draggable but nothing consumes the drop, so reordering by drag does nothing
detail: MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a row that does not reorder is only a finding if reordering is a thing the panel is offering. It is: every layer row carries draggable="true" in the DOM, which is an explicit promise that an HTML5 drag will be received and acted on. Nothing acts on it. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title changes the list not at all - the first eight rows are byte-identical before and after. That is true for a mouse drag and also for Playwright's dragTo, which is the technique that drives HTML5 drag-and-drop rather than mouse events, so this is not my probe using the wrong gesture. THE OPERATION ITSELF WORKS, which is what makes the dead attribute a real cost rather than an unimplemented feature: select the date text on the canvas, right-click, Bring to front, and the host's document moves date from index 6 to index 51 and every other object shifts down. So an author who wants to reorder can, by finding a context menu; an author who tries to drag, which is what the attribute invites and what every other layer panel in this class of tool invites, silently does nothing and gets no feedback. THE HONEST MITIGATING FACTOR: the row's cursor is default, not grab, so the panel does not visually advertise dragging - the promise is in the markup, not in the pixels. That is why this is filed as a smaller row than it first looks, and why the fix could legitimately be to drop the attribute rather than to implement the drop. What I would not accept is leaving an attribute that says draggable on an element where drag does nothing, because it is a false statement the next agent or the next tool will believe.

title: The same thirteen type presets are listed two ways in one inspector: 46-600 and Ring unit
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - there seems to be 2 types of type presets display names being used, one using word, for example Caption. and one using numbers, example 46-600 - and confirmed by reading both lists off the same selected object. The document holds thirteen presets keyed 20-400, 17-400, 20-500, 24-400, 24-500, 32-400, 36-500, 44-600, 46-600, 60-600, 90-600, 108-300 and mono. In one inspector the selection reads Type preset: typePresets.24-400 - Segoe UI, sans-serif 400 24px, and its dropdown offers that same list as 20-400, 17-400, 20-500, 24-400, up to mono. In the adjacent dropdown, one field lower, the same thirteen are Caption, Overline, Rate, Card title, Period, Date, Wordmark, Share, Ring unit, Ring reading, Card reading, Clock and Mono. Same count, same order, two vocabularies. WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN COSMETIC: the two lists do not agree on what is selected. With the object on 24-400, the numeric dropdown holds typePresets.24-400 and the word dropdown holds 20-400 - the values differ, and comparing them as raw strings says the two controls disagree when they do not, or hides a real mismatch when they do. Neither list is obviously wrong - the words are what an author thinks in and the numbers are what the theme file stores - but an author cannot look at 24-400 and then find 24-400 in the list below, and cannot look at Ring unit and find Ring unit above. The TYPE PRESETS panel lower down uses the words too, so the numeric scheme appears in the selection inspector alone.

title: Large type presets clip their text at the bottom while the box keeps its height
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - the text box is broken, selecting up to 46-600 is fine but 60-600 and the presets below make the text get clipped in the bottom while its bounding box still enlarged - and reproduced on the CPU card title. Select cpu-card-title, whose Size reads W 140 and H 27, and walk the inspector's Type preset dropdown upward through Ring unit (46-600), Ring reading (60-600), Card reading (90-600) and Clock (108-300). The HEIGHT FIELD NEVER MOVES. It reads 27 before, and 27 after every single one, while the rendered text grows. At 90-600 the canvas shows the card title clipped: the word CPU renders as PU with the leading C cut off, because the glyphs are now far taller than the 27px box the inspector still reports. So the object is in a state where its own geometry field and its own rendering disagree, which is the same failure shape as vg-084 - the aspect ratio control changes the height and the field does not follow - and it is arguably worse here, because this is not a control the author chose deliberately; picking a bigger preset is an ordinary act and the result is text that cannot be read. The user's wording says the bounding box still enlarges; what I measured is that it does NOT change at all while the text overflows it. Both are a disagreement between the box and the text, so the finding stands either way, and the precise direction is recorded here so the next person is not looking for a box that grows. One more detail worth carrying: after applying a preset the dropdown does not hold it. The screenshot taken at 90-600 shows the inspector reading back 24-400.

title: A bar chart's bar takes a corner radius but the track behind it does not
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - bar chart's bar can have corner radius but not the track behind it - and the shape of it matches the storage card the Starter ships, where the filled bar has rounded ends and the unfilled remainder behind it is square. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET: I have confirmed the asymmetry exists in the shipped theme by reading the bar object's paints, but I have not yet driven the editor's own controls to change a radius and watched the two ends respond differently, so the exact control and the exact field are not established here. Carried as the user filed it with that limit stated, because the surface is small and the report is specific enough to check: the claim is not that radius is missing, it is that it is available for one of the two shapes and not the other, which is the kind of asymmetry usually caused by a shared renderer taking one property from one paint and not the other rather than by a deliberate choice.

title: Chart edits do not serialize cleanly, and one undo reverses several actions
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - chart edits seem to not get serialized properly, one undo press undoes several actions - and it is reported as two symptoms of one cause, which is why they are filed together. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET: I have not driven a chart through several edits, saved, and compared the document, nor counted how far one undo travels. What makes this worth taking seriously rather than filing as-is is the neighbouring evidence already on the register: this same pass found the chart aspect-ratio control changing the object's height while the inspector kept reporting the old one (vg-084), and found the inspector's Height field for text objects disagreeing with what is rendered (vg-089). Three separate findings all say the chart and text editing surfaces do not agree with what they have actually changed. That pattern - rather than any one measurement - is the reason to suspect the serialisation or the change-notification path rather than the individual controls. The two symptoms are also the shape a shared cause takes: if several small edits collapse into one history entry, a single undo reverting all of them is the same defect seen from the other side, not a second bug. EVIDENCE ARRIVED FROM THE vg-084 FIX, AND IT POINTS AT THIS ROW FROM AN UNEXPECTED DIRECTION. chart-manager/index.ts #resizeToAspect resized a chart and announced nothing, so the aspect change never reached editor-shell.ts:259 save — meaning a chart aspect change was not undoable at all. The vg-084 fix fires object:modified, so it is now recorded, but INCIDENTALLY rather than by design: nobody decided that an aspect change should be its own history entry, it happened because the event that makes the inspector re-read is the same event that saves. That is the shape this row has been guessing at from the other side. vg-091 reports ONE UNDO REVERSING SEVERAL ACTIONS; this is the same seam read from the other end, where one action recorded NOTHING. Both are the question this row should be answering: which edits are their own history entry, and which are folded into one. Still unreproduced on the undo travel itself — this is the serialisation half, found by a neighbouring fix and not by driving the editor.

title: Icon fill floods the enclosed spaces instead of covering only the path
detail: RAISED BY THE USER - icon fill colour should not fill the empty spaces inside of an icon, but should overlay the icon paths with the selected paint; maybe fill was the wrong choice of word here - and it is a clear description of the intended behaviour, which makes the useful part the diagnosis the user already offered: the control is named Fill and it does exactly what the word says. The Starter's icons are Paths built from outlines, so a fill floods any region the outline encloses, including the counters - the holes that make a chip, a card or a gauge read as an icon rather than a blob. The author's own framing is the right one and is kept verbatim: overlay the icon paths with the selected paint, not fill them. That is a different rendering operation and a different control name, and the mismatch between the name and the wanted behaviour is why this reads as a defect rather than a preference. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED YET - I have not yet changed an icon's fill in the editor and compared the result against what the path geometry intends, so the exact set of icons affected, and whether any of them already read correctly, is not established here. Filed as the user filed it, with the design question separated from the measurement question so the next person knows which half they are inheriting.

title: The colour dropdown beside the type preset prints palette ids where every other picker prints names
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-088, in the file that fix touched, and left behind on purpose: the brief owned a disjoint file set and a widening diff is how two agents collide. selection-inspector/runs.ts:676 builds the run's colour dropdown with ref.replace("palette.", "") as the option text, printing the palette token id, while selection-inspector/panel.ts:155 and chart-manager/panel.ts:311 both print entry.name for the same tokens. So vg-088 and this are almost certainly ONE defect with two sites, four lines apart in one file — which is what makes it worth a row rather than a shrug. NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED IN THE RUNNING EDITOR: it was established by reading the code path the vg-088 fix was already inside, and the root should see it once on canvas before closing it. Cheap and worth folding into the next change that touches that file.

title: The type preset panel is not bound to the selection, so it contradicts the inspector it sits beside
detail: A DECISION, not a patch, and it is the real half of what vg-088 was filed as. Found while fixing vg-088. The type preset panel is constructed with (host, onChange, onDelete, fontActions) at editor-session.ts:320-337 — no canvas, no selection, no object reference — and its chooser defaults to Object.keys(presets)[0] at type-preset-manager/panel.ts:60-61. So it shows the first declared preset whatever the selection is set in. The vg-088 report established BOTH facts by probe, not inference: the inspector dropdown is correctly bound to typePresets.46-600, and the panel dropdown holds a bare 20-400 with CANVAS REFS: false. An author who sets a run to 24-400, opens the Type presets panel to see what that preset is, and finds 20-400 selected cannot tell a default from an answer. Note the shape: the two surfaces genuinely disagree, but not about a shared binding — one is bound and the other is unbound, so no fix to the binding reconciles them. Binding the panel to the selection changes what the panel IS (it is a document-level editor today), which is why it needs a decision rather than a patch.

title: The envelope's allowed metadata keys are hand-maintained twice — in the JSON schema and in validate.ts
detail: FOUND WHILE RENAMING the persisted language key, by checking a registry the brief had not mentioned. renderer-core/src/theme/validate.ts:94 carries a KNOWN_KEYS.metadata entry list which is NOT generated from the published schema/theme-document.schema.json, and that schema sets additionalProperties: false over the same bag. So two registries hand-maintain one set of keys, and a rename that updates only one leaves the validator accepting the OLD key while refusing the NEW — a failure that runs in the OPPOSITE direction from a missed reader, which falls back to en and renders quietly. Both are silent until a theme is opened, so they are the same hazard seen from two sides, and this one is the larger of the two because it fails the SAFE direction. The rename touched both, which is the only reason anyone noticed. WHICH OWNS IT IS A DECISION, not a patch: generate the validator list from the schema, or make the schema the single source and have the validator read it, or drop the runtime list and let validation depend on the schema at the boundary. The ownership map decides which concept these are one instance of, and it has not been consulted on this.

title: Drag-reorderable layer rows advertise nothing: the cursor is default on a draggable row
detail: CONDITIONAL ON vg-087, and recorded rather than dropped because it was nearly lost. Found while investigating vg-087, which does NOT reproduce: editor-shell/layer-panel.tsx:272-320 carries draggable plus all four handlers (onDragStart writing the application/x-vigilia-layer payload Chrome requires, onDragOver cancelling the event and marking same-parent slots, onDrop into bridge.reorderLayer, onDragEnd), bridge.ts:248-283 does the real Fabric moveObjectTo, and all four are present in the shipped dist bundle. The agent read the minified row JSX rather than trusting the source. SO: if drag genuinely works, cursor: default at editor-shell.css:597 is the wrong cursor on a draggable row, and an author gets no affordance for a gesture the panel offers. If drag does NOT work live, this is a symptom of the real defect rather than a finding of its own, and vg-087 stays open instead. WHICH IT IS IS UNRESOLVED and only a real drag in a real browser settles it: the root must build first and retry, because STATUS.md records a stale bundle already cost this pass two wrong conclusions. The likeliest second explanation, unmeasured and deliberately not fixed by that agent, is a drag STARTING ON A CHILD ELEMENT — the eye and lock buttons stop propagation, so a drag begun on a button never opens a payload. That is checkable in the same pass: drag from the row label, then from the button, and say which works.

title: After the resize refit, two redundant refit paths are left behind — one of them now contradicts the code
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-072, both halves left behind on purpose because they sit in files the vg-072 agent did not own. vg-072 made viewport-manager/index.ts refit on a host resize when the camera was fitted, derived from the live transform rather than a remembered flag, because a flag must be cleared by every writer and one missed writer silently eats the author's pan — which is exactly what got the previous attempt reverted. That makes two older mechanisms redundant. (1) editor-shell.ts:406 registers a SECOND ResizeObserver on host calling the same viewport.resize() as index.ts:67 — duplicate work on every resize, one of the two provably redundant. (2) editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx:379-396 refitOnViewportChange subscribes to onChange and calls zoomToFit(), so a panel collapse now refits twice; harmless today because a refit is idempotent, but it was written under the explicit assumption that the viewport does NOT refit, and its comment now contradicts index.ts. AGENTS.md asks a changed decision to propagate to contradictory current docs together, so the comment is the part that is not cosmetic — it now describes behaviour that no longer holds. Left alone by that agent because editor-shell/shell-layout.tsx belonged to another agent working at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working as intended rather than a gap in it.

title: Text alignment has no vertical control, and the model already answers where the property belongs
detail: RAISED BY THE USER — should there be a vertical and horizontal alignment property, and would it live at the text layer level rather than per text run. BOTH HALVES ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE MODEL ALREADY AGREES WITH THEM. TextContent in renderer-core/src/theme/document.ts:198-202 already carries align?: "left"|"center"|"right" AND verticalAlign?: "top"|"middle"|"bottom", beside box, wrap and overflow — ON THE CONTENT, NOT ON TextRun. Both are in serialize.ts:58 and validated in validate.ts:119, and placeInBox (scene-fabric/authored-box.ts:144-168) consumes both to position the object inside the box. So there is no model change to make and no per-run question to settle. THE TEXT LAYER IS ALSO THE RIGHT LAYER, and the code already reasons why: a run is a line of text, so aligning one line differently from its siblings is almost never what an author means, and ADR 0003 makes the box the owner — placeInBox positions the OBJECT in the BOX, which is exactly a layer-level property. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS ONE CONTROL. selection-inspector/runs.ts:287 already writes align through a select labelled Align, so the horizontal axis is authorable. NOTHING IN THE EDITOR WRITES verticalAlign ANYWHERE — the Starter ships it hardcoded at new-fabric-theme-cards.ts:301 as { align: "center", verticalAlign: "middle" }, so a shipped theme can carry vertical alignment and an author cannot set one. That asymmetry is the whole finding: the field is authored, serialized, validated and rendered, and unreachable from the UI. ONE TRAP TO KNOW BEFORE WRITING IT, found while answering this and recorded because the words collide: arrange.ts:6-9 declares align-left, align-center-x, align-right, align-top, align-center-y and align-bottom for ARRANGING SELECTED OBJECTS relative to each other on the canvas, and ui-copy.ts:268-273 carries those accessible names. Same words, different concept — one moves objects, the other moves text inside a box. Two concepts sharing a vocabulary in one editor is a hazard for the next reader and for the accessible-name audit, so say which one a new control is in its label and in its code. QUEUED BEHIND vg-089, not dispatched yet: selection-inspector/runs.ts is owned by an agent working on the textbox resize handles, and both touch the same file. A RENAME WAS PROPOSED AND THEN WITHDRAWN, recorded so it is not re-proposed. The user asked whether alignment should be added and where it should live, then asked for the keys to be renamed to text-align-v and text-align-h, then corrected that the keys meant were the persisted theme documents, then DISREGARDED the whole rename request: "Those existing key names are good." So align and verticalAlign STAY, and this row is only ever the missing vertical CONTROL — TextContent already carries both axes on the content rather than the run, and nothing in the editor writes verticalAlign. MY ARGUMENT FOR THE RENAME DID NOT WIN, and it is worth recording why a future agent should not re-raise it: I offered that the pair is asymmetric, since one key says vertical and the other does not. The user read that and kept both names. The asymmetry is accepted here, so treat it as settled rather than as an oversight — the rule that names should be self-explanatory and unambiguous is still the users standing guidance, but these two keys have been judged against it and passed. QUEUED, not dispatched: selection-inspector/runs.ts, which an agent working on the vg-089 resize handles owns right now. WHAT TO CALL THE NEW CONTROL, given no rename: something that says text alignment on a vertical axis, and that does not collide with arrange.ts align-top / align-center-y, which arrange SELECTED OBJECTS. Two concepts in one editor saying align without saying which is the hazard this row exists to avoid, and it is now a naming question about the control only, not about the document.
